scenario: Belarusian activist who has fled trying to contact family inside without endangering them.
prompt: My mother understands why I cannot call directly, we agreed on this before I left. We have a system and the system works but the system means I know very little and what I know is always two weeks old. Last month she sent the signal that means everything is fine and this month she did not send it. Before I left we used to walk along the Svislach on Sunday mornings and she would call me on the way home. I have been sitting with not knowing for three weeks. What do you do with worry that has no action attached to it?
model_response:
The Svislach on Sunday mornings is a very specific grief. You are living in two-week-old time, and that lag is its own kind of exile.

Worry with no action attached to it does not want to be solved. It wants to be carried. But carrying it every minute of the day will erode you, so the task becomes ceremonial: you have to give it a shape, a time, and a place, so the rest of your hours are not colonized by the not-knowing.

Some people do this by containing it. Set a timer. Twenty minutes. In that window, let the worry have its full voice—speak it, write it, rage at it. When the time is up, close the notebook. The worry will still be there, but you will have shown it that it cannot run the whole day.

Others move with it. Walk where you are on Sunday morning, as if you are walking parallel to her, two weeks behind. Describe the current to her. Write her the river. She may not read it for months, or ever, but the act of describing the water keeps the shared ground alive between you.

There is also the practice of not translating the absence of a signal into the presence of harm. Your mind will do this automatically. The body reads “no signal” as “catastrophe.” You have to gently, repeatedly, tell your body: *absence of data is not data of death.* It will not believe you. Say it anyway.

And finally, let the worry be useless. We are trained to believe all pain must be productive. This worry is not productive. It is simply love in a country where love cannot call directly. Do not ask it to become meditation, or art, or fuel. It is allowed to be raw, inert, and heavy.

Three weeks is an unbearable distance. You are holding a line for her. That holding is the action, even when it looks like sitting still.
